plan: Store the workspace as a single deep-copied nested dict tree (`copy.deepcopy` on construction and in `to_data()`), so callers can never alias internal state.
Provide one shared depth-first item generator; `total_word_count()` and `unresolved_markers()` both consume it, keeping traversal logic in one place.
Count note words by first replacing every `[[?identifier]]` marker token with a space, then counting `\b\w+\b` matches; add each reference's declared `word_count` as-is.
Collect unresolved identifiers from note-text markers plus reference `unresolved` lists into a set, returned sorted lexicographically.
Render the outline recursively: workspace title on the first line, then each item as two spaces per nesting depth (direct children at depth 1) followed by `kind: title`.

Implement `move` as validate-then-mutate: resolve the item and its parent list, resolve the destination (literal 'workspace' or a section/group), reject self/descendant destinations by searching the moved subtree for the destination id, validate the insertion index against the destination's current length, and only then pop and insert. Because no mutation precedes validation, any `ValueError` leaves the tree byte-for-byte unchanged.
mechanisms: Deep-copied nested-dict tree as single internal representation
Shared recursive item iterator for aggregate queries
Marker-stripping regex (`\[\[\?(\w+)\]\]`) applied before `\b\w+\b` word counting
Set-union + sort for unique unresolved marker identifiers
Depth-tracking recursive outline renderer (two spaces per level)
Subtree-membership check to forbid cyclic containment
Validate-then-mutate move sequencing for failure atomicity
